transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Hirst.
Guns, immigration, climate change and more are on the docket
as the Supreme Court opens a new term tomorrow.
Among the many controversies facing the court
is a question that justices have long avoided,
whether it's unconstitutional to ban semi-automatic assault-style weapons.
And here's Nina Totenberg has more.
On the one hand, for instance, the AR-15 rifle
can deliver up to 100 bullets per minute without any enhancements.
On the other hand, there are some 16 million
semi-automatic weapons in the U.S.
and it's unclear, for instance, how a ban would work
without taking weapons away from law-abiding citizens.
There are many other controversies facing the court.
Everything from test cases on public funding for religious schools,
lengthy detention of immigrants without a hearing,
and of course, very likely, questions about the conduct of elections.
Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
As the head of Tennessee's state prison system Frank Strada
resigns over the failed execution of convicted killer Christa Pike
and Governor Bill Lee called for an investigation into what happened,
her lawyer Stephen Farrell says he wants the governor to commute her sentence.
At the very least, the governor should commute Ms. Pike's death sentence
to a life sentence, at the very least.
We don't know what her physical state will be,
but it is clear that she has endured a torturous attempt at executing her
and we had already asked that the governor commute her for many good reasons.
Speaking there on CNN, Farrell says Pike remains hospitalized in a coma
and on a ventilator.
Voters in Latin Americans' largest democracy go to the polls today
in the latest test for leftists in the region,
which has seen a large shift to the right in recent years.
Brazil's incumbent left-wing president is locked in a tight contest
with the son of his rival, the former migrant president convicted of staging a coup.
And here's Carrie Khan has more.
Both say the contest is too close to call between veteran leftists
Luis Anacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro, a current senator.
Lula, now 80, is facing a tough re-election with voters concerned about crime,
corruption, and a faltering economy.
Bolsonaro says if he wins, he will align more closely with President Trump's
anti-drug interventionist policies in the region.
While Trump has not publicly endorsed Bolsonaro,
he says he's watching the contest closely and touts his clout in the region,
which has seen the last seven presidential contests shift to right-wing leaders
that align with the U.S.
Lula says he's willing to work with Trump as partners,
but insists on respect for sovereignty.
Carrie Khan, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
The Trump administration this week is mailing out $500 checks
to about a million Americans enrolled in some private health care plans
through the Affordable Care Act.
It's for people in states who didn't make too much to get subsidies to help with the premiums.
This is NPR.
In Japan, a U.S. Marine is under arrest for allegedly robbing
and killing a woman in Okinawa.
Twenty-year-old Lance Corporal Devon Baller is suspected of killing
Anna Yagi and then taking her wallet and backpack.
He was stationed on Okinawa Island.
Japan's prime minister calls it a brutal and heinous act
and says they've lodged a strong protest with U.S. officials.
Residents in Okinawa have long been frustrated by the burden of hosting American troops,
which have a strong presence in the area.
Violent Israeli settlers have carried out multiple attacks against Palestinians
in the Israeli-occupied West Bank in recent days,
throwing rocks and burning farmers' olive trees.
The increase in attacks coincides with the start of olive harvesting season,
which has become a pattern in recent years, as NPR's Kat Lonstorff reports.
Israeli settlers burned dozens of olive trees owned by a Palestinian family
south of East Jerusalem on Saturday, according to local officials.
The day before, in separate incidents,
Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian farmers near Nablus,
while masked settlers carrying bats also attacked a group of Israeli human rights activists
trying to protect Palestinians as they harvested olives near Bethlehem.
The United Nations has documented significant spikes in settler attacks
in the West Bank during olive harvesting season in recent years,
with an overall rise year over year in general.
Israel says it condemns such attacks,
but there are usually few consequences for the Israelis who carry them out.
Kat Lonstorff, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Most of the Nobel Prize winners will be announced this week.
Tomorrow, the Prize in Physiology or Medicine will be announced.
This message comes from Lisa and their lineup of beautifully crafted mattresses
tailored to how you sleep.
Each mattress is made with eco-friendly materials
and designed with specific sleep positions and fuel preferences in mind.
Go to Lisa.com for up to 30% off mattresses,
plus get an extra $50 off with promo code NPR.
That's L-E-E-S-A dot com promo code NPR
for up to 30% off mattresses plus an extra $50 off.

topics.text: Supreme Court opens new term with cases on guns, immigration, climate change and more
Tennessee prison head Frank Strada resigns over failed execution of Christa Pike
Christa Pike's lawyer Stephen Farrell calls for governor to commute her death sentence
Brazil holds presidential election between leftist incumbent Lula and rightist Flavio Bolsonaro
Trump administration mails $500 checks to million Americans on ACA private health plans
U.S. Marine Lance Corporal Devon Baller arrested in Okinawa for killing woman Anna Yagi
Israeli settlers attack Palestinians in West Bank, burning olive trees during harvest season
Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to be announced tomorrow
